parts:
Hi, 
I have a large dataset in a regression type model and I would like to generate realizations of the posterior predictive distribution for the response variables given certain covariate patterns of predictors. I can do this but not without monitoring the entire dataset which is resulting in massive (redundant) output files. For example I want to monitor y[39300,1:3] (which are set to NAs in the dataset) and don't want all y[1:39299,1:3] as these are all fixed data values.  I've put the full code listing below. 

Any suggestions greatly appreciated! 
thanks.
Fraser 

### code listing end to end 
rm(list=ls())
gc();
load("isaac_m.RData");# provides isaac.m - a BIG matrix

# create empty response (for one covariate pattern) to get predictive distn. 
extraNA1<-isaac.m[1,] # grab first row and set responses to NAs
extraNA1[1:3]<-NA
isaac.m<-rbind(isaac.m,extraNA1) # append to end of data

library(parallel)

this_cluster <- makeCluster(20)

set.seed(10120)
#seeds=1;

run_MCMC_allcode <- function(seeds,dat) {
  
  library(nimble, warn.conflicts = FALSE)

  code <- nimbleCode({
    
    sigma ~ dunif(0, 20)  ## uniform prior per Gelman (2006)
    psi ~ dunif(0,1)    ## prior on inclusion probability
    
    for(j in 1:r){
      beta0[j] ~ dnorm(0, sd = sigma)
    }
  
    z21 ~ dbern(psi) ## indicator variable for each coefficient
    beta21 ~ dnorm(0, sd = sigma)
    z21beta21 <- z21 * beta21
    z31 ~ dbern(psi)
    beta31 ~ dnorm(0, sd = sigma)
    z31beta31 <- z31 * beta31
    z32 ~ dbern(psi)
    beta32 ~ dnorm(0, sd = sigma)
    z32beta32 <- z32 * beta32
  
    
    for(k in 1:c){
      z1[k] ~ dbern(psi)
      beta1[k] ~ dnorm(0, sd = sigma)
      z1beta1[k] <- z1[k]*beta1[k]
      
      z2[k] ~ dbern(psi)
      beta2[k] ~ dnorm(0, sd = sigma)
      z2beta2[k] <- z2[k]*beta2[k]
      
      z3[k] ~ dbern(psi)
      beta3[k] ~ dnorm(0, sd = sigma)
      z3beta3[k] <- z3[k]*beta3[k]
    }
  
    for(i in 1:n) {
    
    # DAG structure for response - 3-dim logistic output
    # Y1 curEczema_EC03x -> Y2 curRhinitis_RH02 -> Y3 curAsthma_WH02
    #  curEczema_EC03x  ---  curRhinitis_RH02  
    #  curEczema_EC03x  ---  curAsthma_WH02 
    #  curRhinitis_RH02  ---  curAsthma_WH02 
    # can't resolve to use
    # curEczema_EC03x  ->  curRhinitis_RH02 -> curAsthma_WH02 
    # curEczema_EC03x  ----------------------> curAsthma_WH02
    
    
     logit(p1[i]) <- beta0[1] + inprod(z1beta1[1:c], x1[i, 1:c]) # Eczema
     y[i,1] ~ dbern(p1[i])
     
     logit(p2[i]) <- beta0[2] + inprod(z2beta2[1:c], x1[i, 1:c]) + z21beta21*y[i,1] # Rhinitis
     y[i,2] ~ dbern(p2[i])
     
     logit(p3[i]) <- beta0[3] + inprod(z3beta3[1:c], x1[i, 1:c]) + z31beta31*y[i,1] + z32beta32*y[i,2] # Asthma
     y[i,3] ~ dbern(p3[i])
     
     }
   })

  isaac.m=dat[[1]];
  
constants <- list(n = nrow(isaac.m), c=13, r=3, x1 = isaac.m[,c("RF09_01",
                                                                        "RF09_02",
                                                                        "RF09_03",
                                                                        "RF09_01x",
                                                                        "RF10_01",
                                                                        "RF10_02",
                                                                        "RF10_03",
                                                                        "RF10_01x",
                                                                        "RF09101x",
                                                                        "RF09102x",
                                                                        "RF09103x",
                                                                        "RF09104x",
                                                                        "DC01" )])

data <- list(y = isaac.m[,c("curEczema_EC03x","curRhinitis_RH02","curAsthma_WH02")])

inits <- list(beta0 = rep(0.1,3), beta1 = rep(0.1,13),beta2 = rep(0.4,13),beta3 = rep(0.5,13), beta21=0.1,beta31=0.2, beta32=0.2,
              z21=0,z31=0,z32=0,z1=rep(0,13),z2=rep(0,13),z3=rep(0,13),
              sigma=1,psi=0.1)

model <- nimbleModel(code, constants = constants, data = data, inits = inits) # build model


mcmcConf <- configureMCMC(model,print=TRUE) # assign default samplers to nodes
mcmcConf$addMonitors('y[39300,1]','beta0','beta1','beta2','beta3','beta21','beta31','beta32','z21','z31','z32','z1','z2','z3',
                     'z21beta21','z31beta31','z32beta32','z1beta1','z2beta2','z3beta3','sigma','psi')

configureRJ(mcmcConf,
            targetNodes = c('beta1','beta2','beta3','beta21','beta31','beta32'),
            indicatorNodes = c('z1','z2','z3','z21','z31','z32'),
            control = list(mean = 0, scale = .2))

mcmcConf$printSamplers(c("z3[6]", "beta3[6]"))

myMCMC <- buildMCMC(mcmcConf)

Cmodel <- compileNimble(model,resetFunctions = TRUE)
CmodelMCMC <- compileNimble(myMCMC, project = Cmodel,resetFunctions = TRUE)

results <- runMCMC(CmodelMCMC, niter = 200000,thin=20,nchains=1,setSeed=seeds,
                   samplesAsCodaMCMC = FALSE)



return(results);
}

chain_output <- parLapply(cl = this_cluster, X = 1:20, ## NOTE this is the seeds argument!
                          fun = run_MCMC_allcode, 
                          dat=list(isaac.m) # this is one extra argument
                          )

# It's good practice to close the cluster when you're done with it.
stopCluster(this_cluster)

Hi Fraser,

A couple thoughts here:

1) Rewrite the names in the model such that y[39300,1:3] is not part of 'y', but has its own variable name.

2) Don't include y in the monitors. Instead sample from the posterior predictive after the MCMC is done, using R code that makes use of the model and the MCMC output or writing a nimbleFunction that makes use of the model and the MCMC output. This would require monitoring any nodes that are directly involved in the posterior predictive distribution(s) of interest.

-chris

parts:
I was just sketching out the second idea Chris shared:

One option is you could do what you want with a separate nimbleFunction.  Something like this (untested) seems like what you are describing:

predictorNF <- nimbleFunction(
  setup = function(model, input_nodes, output_nodes) {
     update_nodes <- model$getDependencies(input_nodes)
     length_output_nodes <- length(model$expandNodeNames(output_nodes, returnScalarComponents=TRUE))
  },
  run = function(MCMCmatrix = double(2)) {
    m <- dim(MCMCmatrix)[1] # number of saved MCMC iterations
    outputMatrix <- matrix(nrow = m, ncol = length_output_nodes)
    for(i in 1:m) {
       values(model, input_nodes) <<- MCMCmatrix[i,] # You'll need to be sure the order of input_nodes matches the column order of MCMCmatrix
       model$calculate(update_nodes) # update anything that depends on input_nodes
       model$simulate(output_nodes) # insert "includeData = TRUE" if you need to simulate new values into data nodes
       outputMatrix[i, ] <- values(model, output_nodes)
       return(outputMatrix)
       returnType(double(2))
    }
  }

# input_nodes is a vector of node names of the parameters you want to change for simulations.  E.g these would be a subset of column names in the MCMC output.
# output_nodes is a vector of node names of posterior predictive nodes you want to simulate for each row of the input.
myPredictorNF <- predictorNF(model, input_nodes, output_nodes)
# please run uncompiled for debugging
myPredictorNF$run(MCMCsamples)
# then compile
CmyPredictorNF <- compileNimble(myPredictorNF, project = model)

Again, this is untested.  I'm hoping it conveys the idea of what you'd want to do.

-Perry

Fraser, it looks like you're already on the right track.  I'll just re-mention, that Chris's first suggestion ("Rewrite the names in the model such that y[39300,1:3] is not part of 'y', but has its own variable name") is a really dead-simple and easy way to go.  Implementing that strategy would look like:

code <- nimbleCode({
    .....
    yPred[1:3] <- y[39300,1:3]    ## add this line to your model code
})

Then, when you add MCMC monitors (mcmcConf$addMonitors), don't add any monitors to any parts of "y", and instead:

mcmcConf$addMonitors(..., "yPred")

That's all you'd need to do.  This approach has the added cost of adding 3 more nodes (actually only 1 node, a length-3 vector) to your model, which is not a large overhead when compared to everything else going on.  And it has the advantage of simplicity.

Cheers,
Daniel

On Thu, Dec 31, 2020 at 11:40 AM Daniel Turek <db...@williams.edu> wrote:
Fraser, it looks like you're already on the right track.  I'll just re-mention, that Chris's first suggestion ("Rewrite the names in the model such that y[39300,1:3] is not part of 'y', but has its own variable name") is a really dead-simple and easy way to go.  Implementing that strategy would look like:

code <- nimbleCode({
    .....
    yPred[1:3] <- y[39300,1:3]    ## add this line to your model code
})

Then, when you add MCMC monitors (mcmcConf$addMonitors), don't add any monitors to any parts of "y", and instead:

mcmcConf$addMonitors(..., "yPred")

That's all you'd need to do.  This approach has the added cost of adding 3 more nodes (actually only 1 node, a length-3 vector) to your model, which is not a large overhead when compared to everything else going on.  And it has the advantage of simplicity.

Cheers,
Daniel
